name: Pentobarbital
toxicity: potentially lethal when mixed with depressants like alcohol or opioids
summary: A CNS depressant drug that is of the barbituate class. The drug is not used often used medically due to it's high overdose potential in contrast to a lesser overdose risk with benzodiazepine. The drug is used for the treatment of insomnia
advisory: Avoid: All other CNS depressants. It is additionally recommended to be avoided if one has respiratory or liver issues as barbiturates are harsh on the liver.

pharmacology.text: Like other barbiturates, pentobarbital binds to the barbiturate-binding site on the GABAA receptor. This action increases the duration of ion-channel opening. At high doses, pentobarbital is capable of opening the ion channel in the absence of GABA.

uses.text: Pentobarbital is a short-acting barbiturate typically used as a sedative, a preanesthetic, and to control convulsions in emergencies. It can also be used for short-term treatment of insomnia but has been largely replaced by the benzodiazepine family of drugs. It is frequently used for veterinary euthanasia, and is used by some US states and the United States federal government for executions by lethal injection.
